key_insight: DiffSequence-Q uses quantum auxiliary supervision during training to improve protein generation conditioned on secondary structure and solubility, while keeping generation entirely classical.
engineering_relevance: The hybrid design integrates quantum learning into a Transformer-based diffusion training pipeline without requiring quantum computation at generation time.
method: Condition multinomial diffusion on per-residue secondary structure and a continuous solubility target.
Attach a QNN or QKAN solubility prediction head to shared Transformer representations and jointly optimize auxiliary and diffusion losses.
Generate protein sequences using classical reverse diffusion.
evidence_signal: On CATH, DiffSequence-Q led four evaluated models in secondary structure recovery for complete sequence generation; the best QNN and QKAN configurations achieved 14.0% and 22.7% higher mean predicted solubility than the MLP baseline, respectively, with biological activity demonstrated in three protein families.
watch_item: Solubility gains were measured by a separately trained predictor, and the abstract does not establish quantum hardware efficiency or computational advantage.
paper_title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
